title: Unit 8 · The neighborhood
description: Places in town, hay and estar, location prepositions, asking for places, and simple directions.
source: Original exercises aligned to the Aula Internacional Plus 1 Unit 8 syllabus; no textbook exercise text copied.

cards.translation: I buy food at the supermarket.
cards.note: El supermercado is the supermarket.

cards.translation: I buy medicine at the pharmacy.
cards.note: La farmacia is the pharmacy.

cards.translation: I buy bread at the bakery.
cards.note: La panadería is the bakery.

cards.translation: I withdraw money from the bank.
cards.note: El banco is the bank.

cards.prompt: Envío una carta desde la oficina de ___.
cards.translation: I send a letter from the post office.
cards.note: La oficina de correos is the post office.

cards.translation: I borrow books from the library.
cards.note: La biblioteca is the library.

cards.translation: The children play in the park.
cards.note: El parque is the park.

cards.translation: The church is in the square.
cards.note: La plaza is a public square.

cards.translation: I buy fresh fruit at the market.
cards.note: El mercado is the market.

cards.translation: I take the metro at the station.
cards.note: La estación is the station.

cards.translation: Doctors work at the hospital.
cards.note: El hospital is the hospital.

cards.translation: The mayor works at city hall.
cards.note: El ayuntamiento is city or town hall.

cards.prompt: En mi barrio ___ un parque grande.
cards.translation: There is a large park in my neighborhood.
cards.note: Use hay to introduce an unspecified place.

cards.translation: There are three bars on this street.
cards.note: Hay is unchanged before plural nouns.

cards.translation: The bank is next to the market.
cards.note: Use estar for the location of a specific place.

cards.prompt: Las tiendas ___ en la avenida principal.
cards.translation: The shops are on the main avenue.
cards.note: Use están with the plural subject las tiendas.

cards.translation: Is there a pharmacy around here?
cards.note: ¿Hay alguna...? asks whether one exists.

cards.translation: Where is the museum?
cards.note: Use dónde está for a specific singular place.

cards.translation: There is no cinema in my town.
cards.note: No hay means there is not or there are not.

cards.translation: There are many restaurants downtown.
cards.note: Use hay with an indefinite quantity.

cards.prompt: La farmacia está al ___ del banco.
cards.translation: The pharmacy is next to the bank.
cards.note: Al lado de means next to.

cards.translation: The café is opposite the museum.
cards.note: Enfrente de + el contracts to enfrente del.

cards.translation: The car park is behind the hotel.
cards.note: Detrás de + el contracts to detrás del.

cards.prompt: La librería está ___ el banco y el café.
cards.translation: The bookshop is between the bank and the café.
cards.note: Entre means between.

cards.translation: I live near downtown.
cards.note: Cerca de + el contracts to cerca del.

cards.translation: The airport is far from here.
cards.note: Lejos de means far from.

cards.translation: The bank is on the right.
cards.note: A la derecha means on or to the right.

cards.translation: The station is on the left.
cards.note: A la izquierda means on or to the left.

cards.translation: The cash machine is inside the bank.
cards.note: Dentro de means inside.

cards.translation: The tables are outside the restaurant.
cards.note: Fuera de means outside.

cards.translation: Excuse me, where is the metro station?
cards.note: Perdone is a polite way to get a stranger's attention.

cards.translation: Is there a supermarket around here?
cards.note: Por aquí means around here.

cards.translation: How do you get downtown?
cards.note: ¿Cómo se va a...? asks how to get somewhere.

cards.translation: Continue straight ahead.
cards.note: Todo recto means straight ahead.

cards.translation: Turn right.
cards.note: Girar a la derecha means to turn right.

cards.translation: Turn left.
cards.note: Girar a la izquierda means to turn left.

cards.translation: Cross the street at the traffic light.
cards.note: Cruza is the informal tú command; cruce is formal.

cards.prompt: Toma la primera calle a la ___.
cards.translation: Take the first street on the right.
cards.note: Tomar una calle means to take or follow a street.

cards.translation: Turn after the traffic light.
cards.note: El semáforo is the traffic light.

cards.prompt: Es un barrio muy ___. Hay poco ruido.
cards.translation: It is a very quiet neighborhood. There is little noise.
cards.note: Tranquilo means quiet or peaceful.

cards.prompt: Es un barrio muy ___. Hay muchos bares.
cards.translation: It is a very lively neighborhood. There are many bars.
cards.note: Animado means lively.

cards.prompt: Está bien ___. Hay metro y autobuses.
cards.translation: It is well connected. There is a metro and buses.
cards.note: Bien comunicado describes a place with good transport links.
